newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's coalition parties meet on tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's coalition parties meet on tax reform.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Friday opened a meeting of the heads of his centre-right coalition parties and their respective parliamentary leaders to discuss the government's planned income tax reform.

As the meeting got under way it seemed increasingly likely that Kohl's coalition would meet this month with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) in a bid to push the tax plan quickly through parliament.

The reform proposed by the coalition of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) and liberal Free Democrats (FDP) calls for a net income tax cut of 30 billion marks in 1999 by lowering tax rates.
But under pressure from the SPD, Finance Minister Theo Waigel this week suggested that part of the tax plan could be brought forward by one year to 1998 if the needed financing could be secured.

While there are still significant differences between the 14-year-old government coalition and the SPD, Waigel's initiative seemed to open the door for serious talks between the two sides, raising hope that a lengthy parliamentary showdown could be avoided.
